extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, administrative law scholars, government agency case-management staff, and researchers studying agency adjudication time and disposition
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction/analysis of administrative-agency case-processing metrics (case age, disposition manner, and time intervals) as reported across multiple federal agencies for fiscal years 1958–1959.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of proceedings - pending buckets
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of cases pending on June 30th broken down by age categories: '6 months or less', 'Over 6 months but not over 12', 'Over 1 year but not over 2', 'Over 2 years but not over 3', and 'Pending over 3 years'. (Presented in Table 2.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 reports these age buckets for many kinds of proceedings and agencies. Footnotes note that age data are not available for some categories (e.g., Social Security and certain Indian probate cases) and that some proceedings were suspended (e.g., pending reconsideration of Communist Party, U.S.A. case), which affects interval counts. Use these buckets to evaluate case backlog and long-pending cases by agency and proceeding type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of proceedings (agency / statutory classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification/classification of proceedings by reporting agency and the statutory authority or named proceeding (e.g., 'CEA cease and desist orders, 15 USC 13', 'Appeals from benefit rights determinations, 42 USC 405', 'Indian probate matters, 25 USC 372,373').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each row groups case counts by 'kinds of proceedings' with cited statutes; this classification is the unit for reporting all age, disposition, and time-interval metrics. When comparing agencies or totals, match identical statutory/proceeding categories across tables. Note some specific categories (e.g., Social Security, Indian probate) may be excluded from particular tables where data were unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition - disposition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings terminated during the year, the manner of disposition is categorized as: 'Agency decision on the merits after an examiner's decision', 'Agency decision on the merits without an examiner's decision', 'Examiner's decision which became final without review', 'Default, consent, withdrawal, settlement, or other form of agreement', and 'Other final disposition'. (Presented in Table 3.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3 provides counts by these disposition categories per proceeding type and agency. Footnotes explain that the 'consent/agreement' column is intended to include acquiescence or agreement and may also include dismissals for procedural defects; other footnotes list reasons for counts (dismissed as moot, consolidated, not timely filed, failure to file statements of reasons, etc.). These caveats should be considered when interpreting 'consent/withdrawal' versus substantive dismissals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall time from commencement to agency final decision - closed buckets
rubrics_metrics.description: For cases closed by final decision, overall elapsed time from commencement to agency final decision is reported in buckets: 'Closed in 6 months or less', 'Over 6 months but not over 12', 'Over 1 year but not over 2', 'Over 2 years but not over 3', and 'Over 3 years'. (Presented in Table 4.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these buckets to assess how long cases take to reach final agency decisions. Footnotes note data limitations (e.g., FCC consolidated data, some categories not broken down, missing data for certain case types) and that some totals exclude categories (e.g., Social Security, Indian probate). Also note periods of suspension (e.g., Communist Party cases) are included in intervals where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time interval from commencement to completion of hearing (for cases terminated by agency final decision after examiner's decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings terminated in fiscal 1959 by agency final decision after an examiner's decision (Table 5), the time from commencement to completion of hearing is reported in buckets: 'Hearing completed in 3 months or less', 'Over 3 months but not over 6', 'Over 6 months but not over 12', 'Over 1 year but not over 2', and 'Over 2 years'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 5 isolates the hearing-completion interval for a specific subset (cases closed by final decision after examiner's decision). Reported averages (where shown) and per-agency/per-proceeding counts allow comparison of hearing duration across proceeding types. Footnotes clarify which cases are included and any data limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totals and Grand Totals reporting (inclusion/exclusion rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables report totals and grand totals across agencies and proceeding kinds, with explicit footnote caveats about exclusions: e.g., totals exclude Indian probate matters where information not available; some tables exclude Social Security cases; certain counts exclude suspended proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes 5 and related notes explain which categories are excluded from totals. When using aggregate totals, consult footnotes to determine whether particular proceeding types were omitted and whether suspension or consolidation affected counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote caveats on disposition/time classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory footnotes describing special interpretations and exceptions for columns — for example, the 'consent/withdrawal' column includes acquiescence or agreement but may also contain dismissals for procedural defects; 'dismissed as moot' or 'dismissed for procedural deficiency' are sometimes noted; consolidated proceedings; proceedings suspended; not timely filed; failure to file statement of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes provide necessary interpretive rules for reading the tables and reconciling counts. Any analysis must incorporate these caveats to avoid misclassifying dispositions or time intervals. Examples in footnotes show how specific agency-reported items were classified.
